nodes.description: Missense variants in catalytic regions produce full-length RPB1 that still assembles into Pol II but transcribes at reduced rates and with reduced fidelity, proposed to block wild-type Pol II on the same template, a dominant-negative effect. These variants give the more severe phenotype. The elongation-block step is the authors' proposal, not directly shown.

nodes.description: Disturbed RNA polymerase II-dependent transcription during development, probably most consequential in the brain, is proposed to cause delayed or deficient myelination, white-matter loss, thin corpus callosum and cerebellar atrophy, producing the neurodevelopmental phenotype. The tissue-level mechanism is inferred; no patient transcriptomic data exist.

nodes.description: Early truncating variants yield a truncated RPB1 that cannot assemble with Pol II, reducing the level of functional polymerase from the normal allele. These variants give the mildest phenotype.
